http-status.name: HTTP Status Codes
http-status.description: Every HTTP status with a plain-language one-liner — searchable by code, name, or class.

mime-lookup.name: MIME Types
mime-lookup.description: Extension ⇄ content-type lookup with copy-ready values.

ui.noMatches: No matches — try a code, a word, or a class like 4xx.

status.100: Keep going — the server got the headers and wants the body.
status.101: The server agrees to switch protocols (e.g. to WebSocket).
status.200: Success — the request worked and the response carries the result.
status.201: Created — a new resource now exists (usually with its URL in Location).
status.202: Accepted — queued for processing, not finished yet.
status.206: Partial content — a byte range, used by downloads and video seeking.
status.301: Moved permanently — update links; browsers cache this hard.
status.302: Found — temporary redirect; keep using the original URL.
status.303: See other — fetch the result with GET at another URL.
status.304: Not modified — your cached copy is still good.
status.307: Temporary redirect that keeps the method and body.
status.308: Permanent redirect that keeps the method and body.
status.400: Bad request — the server can't parse or accept what was sent.
status.401: Unauthenticated — log in (the name is misleading).
status.402: Reserved for payment flows; some APIs use it for quota.
status.404: Not found — the URL doesn't map to anything.
status.405: Method not allowed — e.g. POST where only GET works.
status.406: Not acceptable — can't satisfy the Accept headers.
status.408: The server gave up waiting for the request.
status.409: Conflict — the request clashes with current state (e.g. stale edit).
status.413: Payload too large for the server's limits.
status.416: Requested byte range can't be served.
status.418: An April Fools' classic (RFC 2324) that stuck around.
status.422: Understood the request, but the content fails validation.
status.425: Too early — replay risk during TLS early data.
status.426: Upgrade required — switch protocols to continue.
status.428: Precondition required — send If-Match to avoid lost updates.
status.429: Too many requests — back off (check Retry-After).
status.431: Headers too large — often oversized cookies.
status.500: Generic server crash — the classic 'something broke'.
status.501: The server doesn't implement this method at all.
status.502: Bad gateway — an upstream server answered garbage.
status.503: Unavailable — overloaded or down for maintenance.
status.504: Gateway timeout — an upstream server never answered.
status.511: A captive portal wants you to sign in first.
